judged_text: packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts:168 — (P2, confidence 75) `try { await sendAddGuestsEmails(evt, guests); } catch (err) { console.log("Error sending AddGuestsEmails"); }` swallows email failure and still returns `{ message: "Guests added" }`, so the dialog tells the organizer the guests were added even though they got no email, and that email is their only invite whenever the calendar update above did not reach them.

adjudication.rationale: In `addGuests.handler.ts`, the core mutation (DB update of attendees and `eventManager.updateCalendarAttendees(evt, booking)`) runs before the email send. The `sendAddGuestsEmails` call is wrapped in a `try/catch` that only `console.log`s and then the handler still returns success (`{ message: "Guests added" }`), so the UI will show the success toast even if notification emails fail. That is a diff-grounded reliability/UX/observability issue, but not a clear correctness defect because guests are still added and calendar updates may still succeed. The finding’s claim that email is the “only invite whenever the calendar update above did not reach them” is not verifiable from the diff.
